title: Go: HTTP Server
description: Build a basic HTTP server with routes, query parameters, POST handling, and JSON responses.

steps.title: HandleFunc route
steps.description: Use `http.HandleFunc("/hello", handler)` to register a handler that writes "Hello, World!" as the response using `w.Write([]byte(...))`. Then `http.ListenAndServe(":8080", nil)` starts the server. Print "Server listening on :8080".
hints: Use `w.Write([]byte("Hello, World!"))` to send a response
`ListenAndServe` blocks — print the message before calling it

verification.failureMessage: Make sure the handler writes a response and the server starts.

steps.title: http.ListenAndServe
steps.description: Create a server on port 8080 that handles `/` by returning "Home page" and `/about` returning "About page". Start the server.
hints: The second argument to ListenAndServe is nil (using DefaultServeMux)
Be careful — listen on a specific address like `":8080"`

steps.title: Read query params
steps.description: Create a `/greet` handler that reads a `name` query parameter and responds with "Hello, <name>!". If name is empty, respond with "Hello, stranger!".
hints: Check if the value is empty string to apply the default

verification.failureMessage: Use r.URL.Query().Get() to extract the name parameter.

steps.title: POST handler
steps.description: Create a `/data` handler that only accepts POST. Read the body with `r.Body` using `io.ReadAll`. Return the body content as the response prefixed with "Received: ".
hints: Check `r.Method != "POST"` and return 405 Method Not Allowed

verification.successMessage: POST handler reads the request body!
verification.failureMessage: Read the request body with io.ReadAll(r.Body).

steps.title: Serve JSON response
steps.description: Create a `/api/status` handler that returns a JSON response: `{"status":"ok","uptime":123}`. Set `Content-Type` header to `application/json`. Use `json.Marshal` on a struct.
hints: Create a struct `type Status struct { Status string; Uptime int }`
Use `json.Marshal` and write to the response

verification.successMessage: JSON response served with correct Content-Type!
verification.failureMessage: Set the Content-Type header before writing the JSON body.
